extraction.name: TravelPlanner
extraction.description: A new planning benchmark that focuses on travel planning, a common real-world planning scenario. It provides a rich sandbox environment, various tools for accessing nearly four million data records, and 1,225 meticulously curated planning intents and reference plans.
extraction.creator: Jian Xie, Kai Zhang, Jiangjie Chen, Tinghui Zhu, Renze Lou, Yuandong Tian, Yanghua Xiao, Yu Su
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was crawled from the Internet and accessed via six tools. Queries were constructed using fundamental elements and GPT-4.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Publicly available Internet data, including Kaggle datasets (Flight Status Prediction, Zomato Restaurants, Airbnb Open Data) and Google APIs.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: Prices for flights and driving were generated by multiplying distance by a random factor.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Data was modified by adding, deleting, and altering certain keys and values. Restaurants and accommodations were randomly assigned to various cities and categorized with specific constraints.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Extracted specific fields from datasets while discarding others, and re-calibrated each query's budget using costs from human-annotated plans.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: 20 graduate students were invited to meticulously annotate plans for synthesized queries. A plan is deemed eligible only if it meets all constraints outlined in the evaluation script.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors performed a detailed review of every query and plan, rectifying any errors found. Through multiple stages of human verification, we ensure the high quality of each query.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: TravelPlanner aims to provide an effective benchmark for complex planning in future research, acting as a catalyst to enhance agents' performance towards human-level cognitive capabilities.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Data is derived from publicly available Internet data and does not represent the authors' viewpoints. The definition of commonsense may vary among individuals.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The sandbox data is based on 2022, which can cause issues if agents assume current dates. Commonsense definitions may vary.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating language agents in tool-use and complex planning within multiple constraints. The dataset is divided into training, validation, and test sets.
